blocker.summary: The r399-r431 investigation chain is CLOSED -- no known blocker remains anywhere in the allocator, threading/shutdown, or presentation subsystems. Summary end to end: r413/r414/r415 fixed and verified the r399 allocator double-issue (a prior fix, r366, had an exception-safety gap that silently orphaned a heap-managed buffer, masked by a wrongly-compared sentinel, causing an unbounded overflow). r420-r422/r424 fixed and verified a shutdown hang (a global IRQL mutex left orphaned by an exception unwind), with automated regression coverage added. r427-r430 fixed and verified the presented_frames=0/present=0 gap: VdSwap's host stub never constructed the XE_SWAP PM4 packet a real kernel would (r427); r429's initial PM4-injection plan was abandoned once r430 found the ring's write-index discovery is entirely independent of VdSwap's own cursor argument (matching real Xbox 360 hardware -- VdSwap programs display scanout directly, it's not a ring command); the actual fix calls present_to_offscreen() directly, live-verified with present_count incrementing 1->5. r431 closed the last gap: ac6recomp's own printed presented_frames diagnostic was still showing 0 because diagnostics_.presented_frames was only ever synced inside dead code (NativeRuntime::submit_ring(), r292) -- NativeRuntime::diagnostics() now syncs presented_frames/state from backend_.present_count() at read time (diagnostics_ made mutable; state() routed through diagnostics() for the same sync). Live-verified: presented_frames=5 state=2 (kRunning), identical with and without AC6_NATIVE_VD_TRACE, in both gdb-driven and standalone launches. Native ctest 11/11 (including ac6_native_runtime_tests, which exercises diagnostics() directly), repo gates and root ctest green. Commit-scope note (same situation as r430, caught before committing this time instead of after): native_runtime.h also carries pre-existing uncommitted backlog (r277, r295) this fix is functionally entangled with -- disclosed in the r431 report rather than left undescribed. Separate, still not fixed: HEAD has never been buildable from a byte-for-byte fresh clone (native_vulkan_backend.cpp has no Vulkan linkage in any committed CMakeLists.txt, r424) -- named for a dedicated future cycle, not a blocker for this chain. Named for r432 (not a blocker, lowest-cost open threads if pursued): the real visual content of presents (still a placeholder color clear, not real EDRAM-resolved pixels), or the dedicated Vulkan/pinned-shader-registry backlog audit r424 already named (including its suspect native_vulkan_backend.cpp.new_header_part file). The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched beyond what r422/r430/r431 already swept in -- reports and named tool/source changes for r413-r431 were committed individually.
